correctness.rationale: For k>=4 every specified directed k-cycle fixes exactly k directed two-edge paths on vertex triples, each raising triangle-cycle probability from 1/4 to 1/2; other triples fix <=1 edge and retain 1/4. For k=3 its fully fixed triangle raises probability by 3/4=k/4. Summing (n)_k/k candidate directed cycles of probability 2^-k gives the covariance and mean. The k=3 instance yields Var(T)=3 binom(n,3)/16; Cauchy–Schwarz gives the variance bound. Independent exact program checked 37 identities.

value.rationale: A single all-k finite covariance identity distinguishes the joint fluctuation of cyclic triangles and directed cycles from known one-variable expectation and extremal constraints. The k/4 marked-cycle response holds uniformly from triangles to Hamilton cycles, and provides a relative-variance lower bound k^2/(3 binom(n,3)) valid for every cycle length, scaling as 2/n for Hamilton cycles. This is a natural simultaneous mixed invariant, not a cherry-picked parameter case; it makes no unsupported broader stochastic-order claims.
